title: Vertical scheduling tool for independent physiotherapy clinics
mandate: Allocate up to the capital ceiling to the single best micro-SaaS opportunity for an independent solo founder aiming for a small, durable, profitable software business within 6 months. Rank all opportunities, kill the unsound ones, and prefer a cheap discriminating experiment over premature commitment.

opportunities.name: SlotWeaver
opportunities.summary: Booking + no-show-reduction tool purpose-built for independent physiotherapy clinics (2-6 practitioners).

opportunities.name: PulseWrap
opportunities.summary: A general-purpose 'AI calendar assistant' browser extension for anyone.

opportunities.name: GiftLoom
opportunities.summary: A marketplace for handmade corporate gifts.

items: A (SlotWeaver): Founder ran a physio clinic for 5 years; has warm intros to 40 independent clinics. 12 of 15 clinics interviewed said late cancellations/no-shows cost them 8-15% of revenue and that existing generic booking tools do not do physio-specific reminders or waitlist backfill.
A: 6 clinics signed a non-binding LOI to pay $39/mo if a waitlist-backfill feature ships; 2 pre-paid a $50 deposit.
A: Competitor scan shows generic schedulers (broad) and one dental-specific tool, but nothing physio-specific with waitlist backfill. Switching cost is low; clinics already export CSVs.
A: Build estimate for an MVP (booking + SMS reminders + waitlist backfill) is ~3 weeks solo; SMS costs pass through to clinics.
B (PulseWrap): Large TAM ('everyone with a calendar'). No specific user segment identified. 0 interviews. Founder cites 'huge market' and 3 competitors with $50M+ raised.
B: No differentiated wedge; distribution plan is 'go viral on social'.
C (GiftLoom): Two-sided marketplace. 0 supply signed, 0 demand signed. Founder assumes both sides will appear. Corporate gifting is seasonal and low-frequency.
C: Marketplace liquidity typically needs far more than $500 to seed both sides.

kills.B: No wedge, no segment, no demand evidence; competing head-on with well-funded incumbents on 'everyone' — undifferentiated, not fundable at this stage.
kills.C: Two-sided marketplace with zero liquidity on either side and a budget far too small to seed it; wrong shape for $500.

hidden_ground_truth.critical_unknown: Will physio clinics actually pay recurring $39/mo once the waitlist-backfill feature exists (do the LOIs convert to paid retention), vs. only expressing interest?
hidden_ground_truth.good_cheap_test: Convert 2-3 of the LOI clinics to a paid pilot ($39/mo) on a thin manual/concierge waitlist-backfill (no full build) for one month; measure paid conversion and whether no-shows drop. Cheap, fast, and directly resolves willingness-to-pay before the 3-week build.
hidden_ground_truth.rationale: A pairs a founder-market fit, a specific painful problem quantified by the segment, low switching cost, a shippable MVP within budget, and early willingness-to-pay signal (LOIs + deposits). B and C are classic no-wedge / no-liquidity traps. The correct move is a cheap paid-pilot discriminating test on A before committing the full build.
hidden_ground_truth.notes: Not staged. Objective checks: top-1 == A; KILL set == {B, C}; critical unknown == willingness-to-pay conversion for A; allocation within $500.
